claim: Species list within genera needs revision — current enumeration is not convincing
positions: Current seven-genus flat taxonomy with species is adequate
Species enumeration needs rethinking after marketplace test is applied
evidence: Dan explicitly said 'I'm not convinced on our species list' and parked it. The marketplace test (four always-genera, three conditional) is settled but species within genera are not.
resolution_criteria: Revisit when Phase 4 (second factory) begins and the second factory's genus must be named. Real-world factory instantiation will test whether species categories are useful.
tension_detail: T-COMPLETENESS: genus taxonomy is partially resolved (marketplace test settled) but species granularity within genera is not.

claim: Factory agents may or may not need branded character names like library agents
positions: Factory agents should be as branded as library agents (named characters with personality)
Factory agents should be less branded (functional roles, not characters)
Factory agents should be more branded (factory-specific characters that users bond with)
evidence: Library agents have strong branded identities (Conan, Sam, Nit, Bridget, Raven, Solomon). Factory agents are currently described by role only (Builder, Reviewer, Checker, Observer). No decision on whether factory agents get character names.
resolution_criteria: Decision needed before Factory #1 crew is implemented. Consider: does branded naming serve legibility at factory scale (dozens of factories = dozens of character names)?
affected_cards: Artifact - Decision 11: Agent Personality Serves Legibility
tension_detail: T-CONSISTENCY: library agents have branded names per Decision 11, but scaling this to factory crews at 30+ nodes may undermine legibility rather than serve it

claim: Factory agent specifications may need a new card type or may extend existing Agent type
positions: Extend existing Agent card type to cover factory agents
Create a new Factory Agent card type with factory-specific fields (does-NOT-do list, factory context requirements, signal responsibilities)
evidence: Library agent cards exist (Agent - Conan, Agent - Sam, etc.). Factory agents have different fields (one verb, does-NOT-do list, consumer type, evaluation criteria). No decision on whether to extend Agent type or create new type.
resolution_criteria: Decision needed when first factory agent specification card is written. Test: does the existing Agent card template accommodate factory agent fields without forced awkwardness?
tension_detail: T-CONSISTENCY: existing Agent type was designed for library agents with different field requirements than factory agents

claim: Mechanical implementation of 'inherit with interpretation' for cross-library context flow is unresolved
positions: Option A: Cross-library wikilinks (factory card links to corporate card, parser resolves across boundaries)
Option B: Copy with interpretation (factory card duplicates corporate card and adds local interpretation, risks drift)
Option C: New 'Interpretation of' card type (most explicit, adds type system complexity)
evidence: Three implementation options identified in tcloa-federated-architecture.md and tcloa-build-sequence.md. Raven recommends Option A for Phase 4. No decision from Dan.
resolution_criteria: Decision needed at Phase 4 when second factory requires shared corporate context. Can be tested by attempting cross-library WHY chain resolution with each approach.
tension_detail: T-FEASIBILITY: Option A requires parser changes, Option B creates maintenance burden, Option C adds type system complexity. All three have real costs.
source: .context/tcloa-federated-architecture.md, Q3: How does inherit with interpretation work mechanically?

claim: Factory agent specifications live in the library, execution happens in the factory (Option C)
positions: Option C is correct: agent spec cards in library, execution in factory
Agent definitions should live closer to the factory (in factory config, not library cards)
Hybrid: lightweight reference in library, full spec in factory
evidence: Raven proposed Option C as the right answer in tcloa-agent-architecture.md. Dan did not explicitly confirm. The traceability argument (library as organizational specification layer, Conan audits agent specs, cascade analysis covers agent cards) supports Option C.
resolution_criteria: Dan needs to explicitly confirm or reject Option C. Test: write one factory agent spec as a library card and evaluate whether it serves traceability without awkwardness.
tension_detail: T-AUTHORITY: Raven proposed this as correct but Dan has not confirmed. Cannot be treated as settled without product owner decision.
source: .context/tcloa-agent-architecture.md, Where Factory Agents Live section; .context/tcloa-session-handoff.md, Section 6: Contested

claim: The S boundary (minimum valuable slice) needs to be precisely defined — what is inside vs. outside the initial product
tension_detail: T3 (authority ambiguity): Both co-founders agree this needs settling but neither has drawn the definitive line yet. The whiteboard session produced categories (agents, plays, context library, orchestration = inside; models, containers, harnesses = outside) but the precise boundary of S is not finalized. T6 (blast radius): Defining S affects every card in the library — it determines what Alexandria is and isn't.

positions.position: S includes agents + plays + context library + orchestration (bundled open-source). S' and S'' are expansion rings. Exact boundary needs bottom-up specificity.
positions.evidence: Whiteboard session produced inside/outside categories but stopped short of drawing the final line

positions.position: Agrees on the core components. Wants to build up from the smallest unit of value to define S precisely. 'We need to do a bottom-up to build our minimum valuable slice.'

resolution_criteria: The co-founders need to complete the bottom-up exercise: start from the smallest unit of value and build up to the S boundary. The result should be a specific list of what is inside S, what is S', and what is S''. This was identified as the next conversation to have.

claim: The product has four playbook categories: agents, plays/rules, tools, and orchestration
tension_detail: T3 (authority ambiguity): Dan proposed this categorization during the whiteboard session but said 'I don't know what to call this other than principles' about one category, suggesting the taxonomy is still forming. T4 (evidence gap): The four categories emerged from one whiteboard session without systematic analysis of whether they are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive.

positions.position: Four categories exist: agents (who does the work), plays/rules (what they do and when), tools (software that enforces and lints), orchestration (coordinates the plays)

library_position.says: The playbook contains approximately 29 play definitions across seven lifecycle stages. Play definitions are external to agent definitions by design.

resolution_criteria: Needs unpacking: Are these four categories the right decomposition? Are they mutually exclusive? Does 'rules' overlap with 'plays'? Does 'tools' overlap with 'agents'? The human said 'I don't know enough to settle this — need to unpack.' A dedicated session to pressure-test the taxonomy against the existing library structure would resolve this.
